text:
nina: follow-up from the Stageridge dedicated outage postmortem. quick summary: transient VPC peering resets from their upstream + an on-prem NAT table exhaustion bug caused keepalive failures and short-lived client isolation.
ben: adding logs we captured during the window. saw peer reset bursts at 02:17:12 UTC, 02:19:03 UTC. their router shows `conntrack` thrash around those times.
murali: do we have a pcap? can we point to the exact packet that triggers the reset? customer asked for artifacts to share with their carrier.
nina: uploaded pcap to INC-15010 and attached a small timeline in the ticket. devops-bot: jira/INC-15010 created and linked: https://redwood/jira/browse/INC-15010.
ben: proposed actions: (1) runtime change to tolerate short peering reset during handshake; (2) ops runbook for dedicated customers with tight conntrack limits; (3) customer liaison to request conntrack increase or change NAT policy.
murali: for runtime I can do a small mitigation: treat a SYN+RST within 500ms as transient and retry with capped jitter, avoid queueing background probes that evict KV entries. I'll open a PR. ETA Fri EOD.
jess: ops action: jess -> coordinate with Stageridge infra to request their NAT table bump and confirm maintenance window. ask them to preserve router logs for 72h. ETA 48h.
nina: product/obs: can we get an alert that correlates peering resets + runtime cache evictions? we need a pageable signal for SRE.
ben: i'll draft an alert: rule triggers when peering_reset_count > 5 in 15m && kv_cache_evictions > 100 in same window. post draft here.
murali: small runtime note: avoid exponential backoff that increases memory footprint; prefer capped exponential with itemized retry queue limit. snippet used in our PoC: ```python
async def handshake():
    for i in range(MAX_RETRY):
        await asyncio.sleep(min(0.5 * 2**i, 8) + jitter())
        if try_handshake():
            return True
    return False
```
jess: also: ops-bot created a runbook stub at /runbooks/dedicated/conntrack-guidance.md. devops-bot: runbook created: https://redwood/runbooks/dedicated/conntrack-guidance.md.
nina: ownership matrix: murali -> runtime mitigations (PR + e2e), jess -> customer coordination & log preservation, ben -> observability rule + dashboard, nina -> postmortem doc update & close criteria.
ben: close criteria suggestion: (A) customer confirms NAT limit increased or maintenance done, (B) runtime PR merged and rolled to 10% traffic, (C) alert firing validated and runbook tested in staging.
murali: risk note: runtime change is low-risk but needs e2e with simulated conntrack drops. i'll run test harness and include results in PR.
jess: I'll push for customer consent for controlled peering test; draft plan posted here by morning.
devops-bot: linked board: https://redwood/boards/remediations/INC-15010 and automated checklist created.
nina: timeline recap: customer liaison & logs preserved (48	60h), runtime PR (Fri EOD), alert/dashboard (next Wed), runbook finalized (1 week).
ben: recurring pattern note: we've seen 3 similar customer incidents in last 8 months with different carriers. recommend a quarterly review of dedicated peering postmortems to identify carrier-specific mitigation templates.
murali: agree. i'll add a short RFC if we want a global runtime toggle for transient-peering-tolerance.
jess: ok i'll start scheduling the carrier review with customer ops.
nina: thanks all. please leave a one-line daily update in this thread until all close criteria met. :white_check_mark:
